title: trunk/696e48875b7adf797c9b6acfc58212424baf74df: [CPP FakeTensor] Enter and exit the C++ FakeTensorMode (#203093)
excerpt: Implement CppFakeTensorMode context management with one thread-local stack. Each entry saves its mode and restoration state, including reentries of an active or inherited mode. Exit requires the matching top entry on the same thread, then restores the previous mode and lift flag. Reject subclasses before changing state and reject mixing Python and C++ fake modes. Match Python's dispatch-mode detection by saving and setting its existing activity flag when an entry installs a C++ mode, and restoring the flag on exit. Reentry of an already installed mode leaves the flag alone. Both TorchDispatchMode and CppFakeTensorMode use _set_in_torch_dispatch_mode for this bookkeeping. Temporary suspension leaves the flag unchanged, while installation without enter does not set it, as for Python FakeTensorMode. Keep balanced, reverse-order context exits. The entry stack records the previous activity flag alongside its other restoration state, without adding another per-mode stack. Detection uses the existing Python flag and Dynamo handling. Cover nesting, reentry, exception restoration, temporary suspension, low-level installation and guarded Dynamo reuse for both fake mode classes. Test Plan: Run from the isolated worktree; the ignored runner redirects the editable install's Python imports to that worktree and uses the existing native build: python ../run_tests.py test/test_python_dispatch.py -k test_mode_detection python ../run_tests.py test/test_fake_tensor.py -k test_fake_mode_dispatch_
